name: DuoAttention: Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference with Retrieval and Streaming Heads
problem: Long-context inference holds a large KV cache and does full attention over it, even though many heads in a long-context model are not retrieval heads and do not need the full cache.
mechanism: Split heads into RETRIEVAL heads (which must keep the full KV cache) and STREAMING heads (whose attention is effectively local and which need only a small cache). Head types are identified by a lightweight OPTIMISATION-based algorithm run on SYNTHETIC data - fit a simple objective so that the cache layout maximises the model's output fidelity - avoiding the need for real long-context calibration data, which is often unavailable. Streaming heads then use a small per-head budget while retrieval heads keep everything.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), reported separately for MHA and GQA models: long-context inference MEMORY reduced up to 2.55x (MHA) and 1.67x (GQA); DECODING sped up up to 2.18x (MHA) and 1.50x (GQA); PREFILL accelerated up to 1.73x (MHA) and 1.63x (GQA), with minimal accuracy loss. Combined with quantization, Llama-3-8B decodes at 3.3 MILLION context length on a single A100. Keep the MHA and GQA figures separate - the GQA numbers are uniformly lower and quoting the MHA figure for a modern GQA model would overstate the benefit.
